prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1193; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a report of a collision at an intersection. Insured vehicle was turning left when it struck the claimant's vehicle, which was proceeding straight through the same intersection. Police report requested. Initial contact made with insured, who confirms the left turn and states the oncoming vehicle was approaching at speed.

Entry 2: Claimant reports a wrist fracture sustained in the impact and has retained counsel. All further communication to be routed through the claimant's attorney. Medical authorization requested through counsel. Reserve set for bodily injury pending receipt of treatment records.

Entry 3: Reviewed scene photographs and vehicle damage estimates. Damage to the claimant's vehicle is consistent with a driver-side impact. Insured's vehicle shows front-end damage. Witness statement obtained from a pedestrian at the corner, who states the insured signaled the turn but the claimant's vehicle entered the intersection on a changing signal. Liability remains under review.

Entry 4: Spoke with claimant's attorney regarding the status of the file. Counsel indicated the client is currently in a cast and has been referred to an orthopedic specialist for follow-up. Attorney requested a demand package once treatment concludes. Advised that the claim will remain open pending a review of the police report and signal timing records.

Entry 5: Police report received. It records the insured as cited for failure to yield on a left turn and notes the claimant's vehicle was not cited. Liability assessment updated to reflect probable shared fault, pending the outcome of the signal timing review. Bodily injury reserve reviewed and maintained. Next action: await specialist records and the attorney's demand package.
